source.heading: The pre-build & the build-on-commit hook
source.text:
## The pre-build & the build-on-commit hook

`dist/web-tools.js` is **the pre-build**: the whole `lib/` frozen into one self-booting offline artifact, so a page adopts the library with one import instead of a `gh.load` chain. `dist/app.js` is the app's own: only what `app/index.html` reaches. Both are tracked. See [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-pre-build).

The `gh.load` chain it replaces is the repo's default, not a legacy path. [`docs/loader.md`](docs/loader.md) is the only statement of the contract a file must honor to be loadable that way, plus the timing invariants the boot sequence depends on. Read it before adding a file to `lib/` or changing how a page boots. Which folder the file belongs in is answered in [`docs/code-layers.md`](docs/code-layers.md) and measured by `npm run code-scan`.

Every **deterministic** derived artifact is owned by one commit-time hook, [`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit). Before a `git commit` it regenerates and stages, in the same commit, whatever the pending changes touch. [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-refresh-model) lists the legs, the order they run in, and why that order matters.

Don't hand-edit a file the hook writes; edit the source and let the hook refresh it. Thumbnails (`pages/thumbs/*.png`) are the exception (see "Per-session refresh" above).

**Git owns the hook, not Claude:** a `PreToolUse` hook disappears when the session root sits above this repo. Run `npm run setup` once per checkout for hooks, the CSV merge driver, and dependencies; `npm run ready` checks without writing. Claude's startup scripts delegate to that shared path. `--no-verify` bypasses it. Details: [extending.md](docs/environment/extending.md).

**Verification stays independent.** Setup never regenerates tracked artifacts, and API, MCP, or server-side writes cannot run local hooks. [`node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs`](node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs) therefore checks every generator under `npm test`. Repair hook-owned output with `npm run artifacts:refresh`, then run any additional command the test names. A local merge that restamps its combined index pauses for the gated `git -c core.editor=true merge --continue` path.

[`.github/workflows/test.yml`](.github/workflows/test.yml) runs `npm test` on every pull request and reports it as a check on the PR, so the test speaks even when no session runs the suite. `page-measures.yml` also runs on pull requests that touch a page, but only reports: a finding never fails it, so a red run is a fault in the pass, not in a page. The suite is browser-free by construction (`node --test` globs `node/test/**/*.test.mjs`, and every Playwright-driven check is named without `.test.`), so keep it that way or the runner grows a browser install. `package-lock.json` is gitignored, so CI resolves dependency ranges fresh on each run and a green check is not a claim about a pinned tree.

problems.note: The heading calls it the build-on-commit hook, P4 the commit-time hook, P5 and P6 the hook; CLAUDE.md elsewhere says the commit hook. Nothing links the heading's name to P4's.

node/README.md#the-pre-build says third-party libraries (Tailwind, daisyUI, Phosphor, Alpine, CodeMirror) stay on their CDN tags, and its comparison line reads 'whole library, one fetch, no own-code network'. 'Offline' promises more than the file delivers.
The chain is never explained. docs/loader.md: a loader-based page calls gh.load(...) once per component and kit, and each file is fetched and run at runtime.
'Reaches' is node/README.md's term of art and 'what' has no noun: the set is lib files only, found by string-literal paths and x-data component names, transitively.
It says nothing about why the two files are committed or what keeps them current. The hook that does is introduced two paragraphs later, and P4 never says the dist files are among its artifacts.
'it' has no single referent: the previous sentence is a pointer to node/README.md, and the candidates are dist/web-tools.js, dist/app.js and the pre-build.

problems.quote: Which folder the file belongs in
problems.note: 'The file' has no single referent: the previous sentence is about adding a file to lib/, so the folder is already named. docs/code-layers.md decides among lib/, lib/kits/, lib/alpineComponents/, lib/ops/, python/ and node/.

docs/code-layers.md calls code-scan advisory: it counts, per folder, the files any document names and any test exercises (python/unclaimed-code.py). It does not check placement. Placement is checked by python/code-shape.py (npm run code-shape) through node/test/code-layers.test.mjs.

The term is never defined here; the reader has to guess it means P2's dist files. node/README.md#the-refresh-model defines the split: a derived artifact is refreshed one of two ways, by whether its generator is deterministic.
'Legs' is never introduced. They are the hook's separate regeneration steps, headed '# --- leg' in .githooks/pre-commit and tabulated in node/README.md.

problems.quote: Don't hand-edit a file the hook writes
problems.note: Too broad: node/README.md#the-refresh-model says docs/docs.csv, docs/harness.csv, docs/registries.csv and docs/tests-authored.csv are hand-edited except for the fields or rows a generator writes.

The exception is to nothing stated. After 'Don't hand-edit' it reads as leave to hand-edit PNGs; the rule it excepts is P4's claim that the hook owns every deterministic derived artifact. Thumbnails are not deterministic, so the hook only warns (.githooks/pre-commit, leg thumb-nudge).

problems.quote: a `PreToolUse` hook disappears when the session root sits above this repo
problems.note: The reader is not told what a PreToolUse hook is, that this hook was one until 2026-08-06, or what the session root is. As written the clause is a non-sequitur after 'Git owns the hook'. 'Session root' and 'project root' (node/README.md) also name one thing twice.
Which driver is not said. It is derived-csv, registered by npm run setup and named in .gitattributes (node/README.md#the-refresh-model).

'Path' reads as a file path. It means the setup code that npm run setup runs: session-githooks.sh and session-start.sh call node/checkout-setup.mjs (docs/environment/extending.md#sessionstart-checkout-delegates).
'it' could be the shared path of the previous sentence, and the flag is bare. It is `git commit --no-verify` and it bypasses the hook.
Independent of what is never said. The next two sentences show it is independent of the hook and of setup, which may not have run.

One kind of file has four names in this section: 'derived artifact' (P4), 'a file the hook writes' (P5), 'tracked artifacts' and 'hook-owned output' (P7). 'Setup' is also the unglossed npm run setup of P6.

node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs holds twelve --check tests. The console build, tests registry, docs registry and CSV census are pinned by node/test/console-suite.test.mjs, tests-registry.test.mjs, docs-registry.test.mjs and csv-census.test.mjs, so the file does not check every generator, though the suite does.

problems.quote: A local merge that restamps its combined index pauses for the gated
problems.note: 'Restamps', 'combined index' and 'gated' are undefined, the agent that restamps (the hook) is left out, and the sentence is about the hook's behavior in a merge, not about verification. node/README.md#the-refresh-model ('Automatic local merge commits use the same order') owns it.

A pull request that cannot merge has no merge ref, so no pull_request run starts (test.yml header, PR #413). The workflow also runs on pushes to main and to session branches (claude/**, codex/**, gemini/**, agent/**), which is the backstop.

problems.quote: so the test speaks even when no session runs the suite
problems.note: 'The test' here is the whole suite (`npm test`), but in P7 'the test' is the one file derived-artifacts.test.mjs; 'speaks' is figurative and 'the suite' follows in the same clause.

problems.quote: a finding never fails it, so a red run is a fault in the pass, not in a page
problems.note: Never says what page-measures does, what a finding is, or what the pass is. .github/workflows/page-measures.yml: it renders touched pages in headless Chromium and reports sideways scroll, blank icons, empty tables and the like; it goes red only when the pass itself is broken.

problems.quote: or the runner grows a browser install
problems.note: 'The runner' could be node's test runner; it means the CI machine, and 'grows' is figurative. The install step would have to download a browser.

problems.quote: a claim about a pinned tree
problems.note: 'Pinned tree' is jargon for a fixed set of dependency versions, which a lockfile would give. .github/workflows/test.yml: no lockfile to npm ci against.

session-root.gloss: The project root of a Claude Code session. A session spanning several checkouts has its root above all of them, so none of their .claude/settings.json hooks fire.
